Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
914 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Major to moderate tidal flooding is ongoing and will continue
through Friday. Rain and wind impacts have come to an end across
the region. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Moderate to Major tidal flooding persists through Friday. 

- 2) Dry conditions Sunday, followed by precipitation Sunday
  night and early Monday, then dry again Monday afternoon
  through Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Moderate to Major tidal flooding persists
through Friday. 

Evening update...The large cutoff low over the southern
Appalachians this evening will slowly continue pushing
north/east tonight. The region remains socked in a strong CAD
from the very strong surface high over New England. The main
surface low has now departed well to our north, so all of the
rain and wind from earlier has passed through. A lingering heavy
mist slowly wanes overnight as southwesterly flow increases.

Previous Discussion...

Latest sfc observational trends and LWX VWP showed that sfc 
winds and winds aloft have likely peaked across the area as low
pressure center nears the area. The strongest gust seen so far
today was at DCA with a gust to 54 kt (62 mph) at 1020 AM. The 
low pressure center is currently located near Ladysmith VA and 
will move north into Pennsylvania by 06Z tonight. The bulk of 
the rain will move north of the Washington metro area by 4 PM, 
but linger longer across northeast MD until about 7-8PM. A lull 
in precip will occur this evening as mid-level dry slot moves 
in. Overnight, upslope showers will return to the mountains with
rain turning into snow showers around daybreak Fri. 

Heading into Friday, the focus shifts to the Allegheny Front as
an extended period of upslope aided rain/snow showers will 
occur. Deep-layered westerlies are not the most ideal with 
upslope, but net snow accumulations around an inch or two are in
the forecast. Otherwise, the big story for the day will be 
another round of brisk winds across the entire area. Initial 
winds start off out of the south on Friday morning before 
shifting over to west to southwesterly for the second half of 
the day. The passage of the upper low should make for an 
expansive stratocumulus deck which offset some of the daytime 
heating. After spending Thanksgiving Day in the 40s and 50s, 
expect much of the same for Friday (30s along the Alleghenies). 
Southwesterly winds will gust around 25 to 35 mph, while 
remaining elevated into Friday night over the higher terrain. 
Westerly gusts overnight could approach 40 to 50 mph along the 
Allegheny Front. 

The powerful Thanksgiving Day system finally reaches the
Canadian Maritimes by Saturday. This will provide increasing
sunshine through the day, much less wind, along with a gradual 
warm up. Saturday's forecast highs are in the 50s to near 60 
degrees, with upper 30s to 40s across mountain locations. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry conditions Sunday, followed by precipitation Sunday night 
and early Monday, then dry again Monday afternoon through Wednesday.

High pressure will keep the region dry Sunday. Temperatures will be 
near seasonable with highs middle 50s to lower 60s.

As the high pushes further to the southeast Sunday night, a low 
pressure system will move from the middle Mississippi Valley on 
Sunday toward the eastern Great Lakes Sunday night. A trailing cold 
front will push across the region Sunday night into Monday morning.
Showers will likely accompany the front. We can't rule out a clap of 
thunder or two either given that there will be plenty of wind shear, 
despite instability being minimal to nil and the time of night for 
frontal passage. Highs cooler Sunday with highs mainly in lower to 
upper 50s.

Once the front moves to the east and southeast Monday afternoon, 
high pressure will become reestablished and bring dry conditions 
and seasonable temperatures to the region Monday through 
Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /02Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
IFR to potential LIFR CIGs have spread across the area and will
persist through most of the night. As southwest winds increase
late tonight that will cause CIGs to steadily rise through the
morning Friday. VFR conditions return, but it is possible some
MVFR CIGs linger through Friday afternoon. The main impact
Friday will be from southwest winds gusting 25-30 knots. VFR
conditions return Friday night into Saturday.

VFR conditions Sunday. MVFR or IFR conditions possible Sunday night 
and Monday morning with front and showers and/or thunder. VFR 
conditions return Monday afternoon and Monday night. Winds variable 
becoming southeast 5 to 10 knots Sunday, increasing south to 
southwest 10 to 15 knots gusts 20 knots Sunday night, shifting 
northwest 10 to 20 knots gusts 25 knots Monday with frontal
passage.

&&

.MARINE...
A lull in winds is ongoing now across the waters. Expect winds
to quickly ramp up tonight as southwest flow increases. Gale 
Warnings remain in place as gusts of 20-30 knots return late
tonight through Friday afternoon. SCA conditions then linger
Friday night into Saturday afternoon before winds decrease 
Saturday night.

Small craft advisories look increasingly likely late Sunday into 
Sunday night with approaching front. Once the front passes later 
Sunday night or early Monday, then Gales could be possible with a 
gusty northwest wind. Small craft advisories look likely. Winds 
southeast 5 to 15 knots Sunday, then south to southwest 15 to 20 
knots Sunday night, shifting northwest 15 to 25 knots gusts up to 30 
knots Monday.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Moderate to major tidal flooding is ongoing at many locations
along the shoreline of the Chesapeake Bay and tidal Potomac
River. Tide levels are expected to remain elevated through
Friday afternoon with Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories
continuing. Water levels slowly decrease Friday night into the
weekend.

&&

.CLIMATE...
After today's heavy rainfall, there are several locations that
have set their wettest Thanksgiving Day on record. This is the
case for Washington DC (DCA), Washington Dulles (IAD), Baltimore
(BWI), Charlottesville (CHO), and Martinsburg (MRB). Final
numbers will be available tonight once the official daily
information is tallied.
